description: Climate TRACE is an independent inventory of greenhouse gas emissions built by a not-for-profit coalition of more than 100 universities, scientists and AI experts, which uses satellite observations, remote sensing and machine learning to estimate emissions asset by asset. On 26 September 2026 the site summarised 2,765,771 emission sources from 744,678,997 assets, grouped into 10 industrial sectors and 67 sub-sectors, for three greenhouse gases and eight other air pollutants, with annual data from 2015 to 2025 and monthly data from 2021. Release 5.11.0 of 24 September 2026 carries monthly emissions through July 2026. Data are free: a download tool by country and sector, custom queries, city and subnational data, geospatial files for selected sectors, a GeoPackage of boundary-based sources, a dataset of top emission reduction strategies and a public API; the data are licensed Creative Commons 4.0 under the project's terms of use. Caveats: estimates are modelled and their accuracy varies by sector, and methods change between releases (changelog on GitHub). For simulation it provides a global asset inventory of emitting industrial plants and other infrastructure with activity-based emissions, for decarbonisation scenarios and exposure studies. Related catalogue records include the Global Iron and Steel Tracker and the European Industrial Emissions Portal.
